newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-EWING'S 30 POINTS LEADS KNICKS PAST PISTONS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-EWING'S 30 POINTS LEADS KNICKS PAST PISTONS.

text.p: Patrick Ewing scored 30 points, including a clutch jumper with 21 seconds to go, as the New York Knicks avenged their worst loss of the season with a 95-92 victory over the Detroit Pistons on Saturday.

John Starks added 17 points off the bench for the Knicks, who have won nine of their last 10 games. The only loss in that stretch was a 112-78 defeat at Detroit on Wednesday in which Ewing scored six points.
"They kicked our butts convincingly in Detroit," Ewing said. "We wanted to come out and make a statement."
Joe Dumars scored 16 points and Lindsey Hunter 13 for the Pistons.
In Charlotte, Dell Curry scored 19 points off the bench and Anthony Mason had 18 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists to lead the Charlotte Hornets to a 98-93 victory over the Atlanta Hawks.
Matt Geiger chipped in 13 points and eight rebounds for Charlotte, and Muggsy Bogues added 15 points.
Christian Laettner had 24 points and Dikembe Mutombo had 20 for Atlanta, which had its five-game winning streak halted.
"We were just a step slower all night and we shot very poorly," said Atlanta coach Lenny Wilkens.
In Houston, Voshon Lenard scored a career-high 22 points as the shorthanded Houston Rockets, held to the lowest total in franchise history, beat the Miami Heat 86-66.
Miami allowed just eight points in the fourth quarter as it snapped an overall two-game skid.
Hakeem Olajuwon scored 20 points for the Rockets, who played without suspended superstars Charles Barkley and Clyde Drexler and lost their third straight game.
In Milwaukee, Glenn Robinson had 24 points and 13 rebounds as the Milwaukee Bucks cruised to a 103-85 romp over the injury-riddled Orlando Magic, who have lost five straight games.

Ray Allen had 16 points and Vin Baker 13 as the Bucks won for the fourth time in six games. erald Wilkins scored 17 points and Horace Grant 16 for the Magic, who have lost nine of their last 10 games.

At New Jersey, Robert Pack had 29 points and Kendall Gill made a layup with 3.5 seconds left as the New Jersey Nets snapped a five-game losing streak with a 101-100 win over the Boston Celtics in a matchup of the Eastern Conference's worst teams.

Gill, who had 24 points, made a driving layup and was fouled by Rick Fox as the lead changed hands for the fifth time in the final two minutes. Gill missed the free throw, but the Celtics could not get off another shot.
Shawn Bradley has his fourth career triple-double with 17 points, 15 rebounds and 11 blocked shots.

In Philadelphia, Michael Jordan scored 31 points and sparked a pair of fourth-quarter runs as the Chicago Bulls won their sixth consecutive game with a 111-105 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers, who have dropped 10 in a row.
Scottie Pippen scored 22 points and Dennis Rodman had 12 points and 18 rebounds for Chicago.

"We'll get better," said rookie Allen Iverson, who broke out of a slump with 32 points. "We're playing as hard as we can and that's all you can ask. Hopefully we can bounce back from this with something positive."
In San Antonio, Sean Elliott scored 12 of his 29 points in the third quarter as the recovering San Antonio Spurs won their third consecutive game with a 101-88 victory over the Phoenix Suns.
Dominique Wilkins scored 24 points and David Robinson added 12 points and 10 rebounds for San Antonio.
At Minnesota, Kevin Garnett had 23 points and Tom Gugliotta had 17 as the Minnesota Timberwolves snapped a three-game skid with a 103-88 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers.
Rookie Stephon Marbury added 17 points and eight assists for Minnesota, which had lost nine of its last 10.
Nick Van Exel totalled 22 points and Shaquille O'Neal 21 for Los Angeles, which had won nine of its last 11 games.

In Sacramento, Mitch Richmond scored 10 of his season-high 37 points in overtime, including an alley-oop basket with two-tenths of a second remaining to lift the Sacramento Kings to a 101-99 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Kings called timeout in the middle of a fast break with 1.8 seconds left. With Billy Owens inbounding, Richmond faked to the foul line, then cut back past Clifford Robinson to the basket, took a pass in mid-air and banked in a scoop shot.
